---
title: "Resources"
---

## Course material

- **Textbook:** [Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces](http://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/) by Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, free online.
- **Course VM:** [Ubuntu VirtualBox image](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jZVQRuomuYsuK5dkTyuVMxV4oNLFX8Hs/view) with the tools used in labs and homework.
- **Recordings:** [YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLftoLyLEwECB3NsNfQ1oxtt8IoBNRWcO5) of the 2018 lectures.
- **Code used in class:** the [code folder](code/index.qmd) on this site.
- **Source of this site:** [nipunbatra/os2018](https://github.com/nipunbatra/os2018) on GitHub, including lab code.
- **Project ideas:** [course project ideas spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eVVmBrCTXHa6XhfewG2S9_if11Ija0s_cNMBp5NMbww/edit?usp=sharing).

## Videos

- [Introduction to memory management in Linux](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7aONIVSXiJ8)
- [Google Chrome and security: sandboxing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=29e0CtgXZSI), on Chrome's multi-process design

## Further reading

- Dennis M. Ritchie and Ken Thompson, [The UNIX Time-Sharing System](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~brewer/cs262/unix.pdf)
- Maurice J. Bach, [The Design of the UNIX Operating System](https://www.pearson.com/store/p/design-of-the-unix-operating-system-the/P100000312857)
- Andrew S. Tanenbaum, [Modern Operating Systems](https://www.pearson.com/store/p/modern-operating-systems/P100002443471)
- [OSDev Wiki](https://wiki.osdev.org/)
- [Linux kernel documentation](https://www.kernel.org/doc/)
- [xv6](https://pdos.csail.mit.edu/6.828/2020/xv6.html), a simple Unix-like teaching operating system ([source](https://github.com/mit-pdos/xv6-public))
- [Minix](https://github.com/Stichting-MINIX-Research-Foundation/minix), a microkernel-based operating system
- [seL4](https://github.com/seL4/seL4), a high-assurance microkernel

## Programming

- Brian W. Kernighan and Dennis M. Ritchie, [The C Programming Language](https://www.amazon.com/Programming-Language-2nd-Brian-Kernighan/dp/0131103628)
- [C reference](https://en.cppreference.com/w/c) on cppreference.com
- [GDB documentation](https://www.gnu.org/software/gdb/documentation/)
- W. Richard Stevens and Stephen A. Rago, [Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment](https://www.amazon.com/Advanced-Programming-UNIX-Environment-3rd/dp/0321637739)
- Robert Love, [Linux System Programming](https://www.amazon.com/Linux-System-Programming-Robert-Love/dp/1449339530)
- Michael Kerrisk, [The Linux Programming Interface](https://www.amazon.com/Linux-Programming-Interface-System-Handbook/dp/1593272200)
- Tools used in the course: GCC, GDB, Valgrind, Make, `top`, `htop`, `ps`, `strace` and `perf`.

## Practice and questions

- [LeetCode concurrency problems](https://leetcode.com/problemset/concurrency/)
- [HackerRank](https://www.hackerrank.com/domains/algorithms) and [Codeforces](https://codeforces.com/)
- [Stack Overflow: operating-system](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/operating-system), [r/AskComputerScience](https://www.reddit.com/r/AskComputerScience/) and [Unix & Linux Stack Exchange](https://unix.stackexchange.com/)
